stories.body: The United States launched a new wave of strikes on Iranian military targets along the country’s southern coast, saying it was responding to attempted attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on US personnel. Iran retaliated with missile and drone attacks aimed at US facilities in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq’s Kurdistan region. Iranian authorities said US shrapnel struck a home hosting a wedding in southern Iran, killing at least four people including a child and injuring dozens; US Central Command said it was aware of the reports but does not target civilians. The fighting marks a sharp renewal of hostilities after a month-long lull, adding to concern over the security of the Strait of Hormuz and the prospect of a wider regional war.
stories.headline: US and Iran Exchange Fresh Strikes Across the Middle East

stories.body: Germany has formally accused Russia of being behind an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in August, when an explosive-laden drone was found near Ukrainian cargo aircraft. Officials said the device’s configuration, police investigation and intelligence findings pointed to Russian responsibility, describing the incident as part of a familiar pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe. Berlin responded by ordering the closure of Russia’s consulate in Bonn, planning to terminate the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin, tightening controls on Russian entry and seeking further sanctions. Moscow denied involvement and said it would respond in kind.
stories.headline: Germany Blames Russia for Explosive-Drone Incident at Leipzig Airport

stories.body: Joshua Wong, one of Hong Kong’s best-known pro-democracy activists, pleaded guilty to conspiring to seek foreign sanctions against Hong Kong and China under the territory’s national security law. Prosecutors said Wong worked with exiled activist Nathan Law and lobbied foreign politicians for sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures. The 29-year-old, imprisoned continuously since 2020 and already serving a sentence for subversion, could face three to 10 years in prison or life imprisonment if the court considers the offence grave. Supporters said the case illustrates the continuing use of the security law to suppress dissent.
stories.headline: Hong Kong Democracy Activist Joshua Wong Pleads Guilty to Foreign-Collusion Charge

stories.body: Nepal has begun burying unidentified flood victims in mass graves after collecting DNA samples, as morgues struggle to cope with the scale of the disaster. Authorities said 1,003 bodies had been recovered and 3,916 people remained missing after a high-altitude glacial collapse on August 26 sent freezing water, rocks and debris through Himalayan valleys. Bodies continue to be found in devastated communities and downstream rivers, including in India, while many remains are too decomposed for immediate identification. The disaster has overwhelmed traditional Hindu cremation and funeral rites.
stories.headline: Nepal Begins Mass Burials After Catastrophic Flooding

stories.body: A global sell-off in government bonds intensified as renewed fighting between the United States and Iran pushed oil prices higher and revived inflation concerns. Investors fear central banks may need to raise interest rates while governments are already facing large debt burdens, driving up borrowing costs across major markets. Britain’s 10-year gilt yield rose to nearly 5.3%, its highest level since 2008, while Japan’s 10-year yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996. Stocks also fell across Asia as Brent crude hovered around $95 a barrel and markets absorbed the risk of further disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.headline: Global Bond Sell-Off Deepens as Iran Conflict Stokes Inflation Fears

stories.body: Massachusetts voters backed several long-serving Democrats in primary contests, led by Senator Ed Markey’s victory over Representative Seth Moulton for the party’s Senate nomination. Markey, 80, defeated the 47-year-old Moulton after running as the more progressive candidate with support from figures including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren. Representatives Stephen Lynch and Richard Neal also turned back younger challengers in their House primaries. The results showed that calls for generational change did not overcome the incumbents’ ideological alliances and established support in the heavily Democratic state.
stories.headline: Massachusetts Primary Elections Preserve Veteran Democratic Incumbents

stories.body: A Politico survey of Republican candidates and lawmakers found that many do not plan to attend, or remain undecided about attending, President Donald Trump’s midterm convention in Dallas next week. Members cited district commitments, personal conflicts and a suggested minimum $25,000 donation for attendance, while some candidates in competitive races were wary of appearing closely tied to the polarizing president. Trump and Vice President JD Vance are scheduled to headline the event, along with senior Republican congressional leaders, but several vulnerable House members and Senator Susan Collins are among those expected to skip it.
stories.headline: Many Republicans Plan to Skip or Remain Undecided on Trump's Midterm Convention

stories.body: Deadly flash flooding in the Grand Canyon has damaged infrastructure, prompted rescues and shut down South Rim lodging indefinitely after a washed-out pipeline cut the area’s water supply. The park remains open, but visitors with long-standing overnight reservations have had to seek accommodation elsewhere, adding economic strain to an area still recovering from a previous fire. Hikers caught in narrow canyon terrain described being trapped by sudden rain and floodwaters, underscoring the danger of the storm system that has already killed two people.
stories.headline: Grand Canyon Flooding Kills Two and Disrupts Tourism Economy

stories.body: A federal judge has ruled that Idaho cannot prosecute doctors who perform abortions to protect a pregnant patient’s health or prevent self-harm. US District Judge B. Lynn Winmill found that the state’s near-total abortion bans violate the Fourteenth Amendment when they force patients to endure serious, nonfatal harm, including severe mental-health risks. The ruling does not rest on a general right to abortion, the judge wrote, but on limits to the state’s power to compel harm for the benefit of a fetus. Idaho Attorney General Raul Labrador said the state would appeal.
stories.headline: Federal Judge Blocks Idaho From Prosecuting Doctors Over Health-Protecting Abortions

stories.body: A Spanish police intelligence report delivered to the National Court concludes that Moroccan security forces, including uniformed and plainclothes agents, planned and guided the mass entry of tens of thousands of people into Ceuta on July 30 and 31. The report says the migration crisis was used as cover for an operation intended to overwhelm Spain’s border-control system and notes that roughly 90% of those who crossed returned to Morocco within hours. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska has demanded explanations from the police director over when the government learned of the report, after officials had previously denied evidence of Moroccan involvement.
stories.headline: Police Report Says Moroccan Agents Guided Mass Crossing Into Ceuta

stories.body: Spain’s government has approved a €309 million emergency plan for Ceuta, seeking to counter local perceptions that the autonomous city has been neglected after its recent migration crisis. The funding includes direct economic assistance, security spending, care for migrants and reinforcement of public services. The announcement comes amid political pressure from Ceuta’s regional president, Juan Jesús Vivas, who has argued that the city needs stronger backing from Madrid.
stories.headline: Spanish Government Approves €309 Million Emergency Plan for Ceuta

stories.body: Spain lost about 163,000 Social Security affiliates in August as seasonal tourism and education employment declined, while registered unemployment rose by 44,419 to 2.36 million. Despite the monthly setback, unemployment remains at its lowest August level since 2007 and employment is still up about 679,000 from a year earlier. The government said an extraordinary migrant regularisation process softened the fall in formal employment, adding nearly 338,000 foreign workers to Social Security rolls, while also contributing to a larger increase in people newly registering as unemployed.
stories.headline: Spain Loses 163,000 Jobs in August as Summer Season Ends

stories.body: The European Public Prosecutor’s Office has informed Spain’s National Court of evidence that a network linked to fuel-sector companies allegedly moved €27.9 million to Portuguese companies between 2022 and 2024 to launder proceeds from suspected VAT fraud. The prosecutors said a company attributed to businessman Víctor de Aldama received more than €7.4 million and that the accounts showed no apparent fuel purchases matching the purported transactions. About €11.8 million has been seized in Portugal, while other funds allegedly returned to Spain or were moved to the United Kingdom and other jurisdictions.
stories.headline: European Prosecutors Link Víctor de Aldama to Alleged €27.9 Million Laundering Scheme in Portugal

stories.body: Catalonia’s Health Department will phase out username-and-password access to the La Meva Salut personal health portal and make idCAT Mòbil its primary authentication method. Both systems will remain available until January 2027, though users will no longer be able to create new passwords from September 15. The government says the change will strengthen protection of medical data by using identity verification and one-time mobile codes, but it has prompted concern from families and advocates for older people, who warn it could worsen the digital divide and complicate access for dependants without smartphones.
stories.headline: Catalonia Will Replace La Meva Salut Password Access With idCAT Mòbil

stories.body: Catalonia recorded its hottest meteorological summer since records began, with average temperatures about 3°C above the 1991-2020 norm across more than 80% of the territory, according to the Catalan Meteorological Service. Some inland areas, the western Pyrenees and the Vic plain exceeded the average by more than 4°C. Barcelona registered 59 torrid nights above 25°C, while Lleida had 15 days at or above 40°C. Much of the region was also dry or very dry, although intense late-August rain made parts of Tarragona unusually wet.
stories.headline: Catalonia Records Its Hottest Summer on Record

stories.body: A 38-year-old motorcyclist died after a car struck him while he was stopped at the intersection of Aribau and Mallorca streets in Barcelona’s Eixample district. The driver fled but was stopped by Mossos d’Esquadra about a kilometre away and arrested by the Guàrdia Urbana. Authorities are investigating the driver for suspected negligent homicide, fleeing the scene, refusing an alcohol test and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The death is Barcelona’s 11th traffic fatality of 2026.
stories.headline: Barcelona Police Investigate Fatal Hit-and-Run That Killed Motorcyclist in Eixample
